title: docs(permissions): name where a high-privilege anchor binding is refused; spec patch changeset for the anchor docblock
body:
Fixes #23887
Fixes #23935
Clause-②: no

## What

The contract review of the anchor-docblock change (`6f7ad7900f`, review `6214176883` on #23373) left two release-text items. This PR handles both:

1. **`.changeset/23887-anchor-docblock-guest-no-door.md`**: `'@objectstack/spec': patch` for the docblock that change landed on `EVERYONE_POSITION` / `GUEST_POSITION` (`packages/spec/src/identity/position.zod.ts:159-167`). The docblock now says packages suggest bindings to `everyone` only and the admin confirms each one, and that no door binds a set to `guest` until ADR-0138 D3 item 5's bind door is built.
2. **`content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx:68-78`**: the page said "The `everyone`/`guest` audience-anchor bindings reject high-privilege sets at the data layer for every caller". That stopped being true when the data-layer gate retired with `sys_position_permission_set`. The new text names each refusal point measured below.

This PR changes no code, no other docs page and nothing under `packages/spec/src/**`. It touches no governed surface.

## Why the changeset is owed (measured on this tree's build)

- `packages/spec/package.json` `files[]` = `["dist","json-schema","liveness","prompts","llms.txt","README.md","src/**/*.zod.ts","CHANGELOG.md","api-surface","spec-changes.json","protocol-upgrade-guide.md"]`. So `src/identity/position.zod.ts` ships in the tarball.
- After `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build`, the new sentence (``No door binds a set to `guest` ``) appears in `dist/membership-role-BpDGLF1o.d.ts` and `dist/membership-role-a9eypi2I.d.mts`. Positive control: the older sibling sentence ("its bindings face the strictest lint tier") appears in the same two files.

## Where a high-privilege set bound to an anchor is refused (measured)

Tree: `packages/**` byte-identical to `origin/main` `5fb8d158b5`. Search: `git grep -n describeAnchorForbiddenBits` gives 38 hits. Only 3 are production call sites, and all 3 pass `everyone`. The other production anchor check is the one `describeHighPrivilegeBits` caller in `security-plugin.ts`. The anchor seal paths were read separately. The line numbers the card gave (`:512`, `:865`) have since moved to `:659` and `:1040`.

| # | Refusal point | Code | Answer | Measured by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Accepting a package `isDefault` suggestion: `POST /api/v1/security/suggested-bindings/:id/confirm` calls `confirmAudienceBindingSuggestion` | `plugin-security/src/suggested-audience-bindings.ts:1040` (`everyone` tier, with the stack's declared capabilities) | `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`; the row stays `pending` and nothing is recorded | `suggested-audience-bindings.test.ts` "refuses a set carrying anchor-forbidden bits — 403, nothing recorded", plus the undeclared-token and platform-capability controls: passed |
| 2 | Each derivation of `everyone`'s definition, acceptance half: `readAcceptedEveryoneSets`, for record rows and for a walled host's `acceptedDefaultPermissionSets` | `suggested-audience-bindings.ts:659` | the set is withheld and reported as `forbidden`; `declareEveryone` logs it at `error` | tests "withholds an accepted set whose published body now carries a forbidden bit" and "a declared name passes the everyone anchor's high-risk gate": passed |
| 3 | Each derivation, baseline half: `everyoneBaseline` (`describeHighPrivilegeBits`, which is the whole `everyone` tier) | `plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts:4755-4765`, called from `declareBuiltinPositions` (`init()`) and `declareEveryone` (`kernel:ready`, and `rederiveEveryone` on accept, revoke, uninstall and package publish) | the baseline set is left off `everyone`, with a `warn` | `builtin-positions.declaration-phase.test.ts` and the `security-plugin.test.ts` block "audience-anchor bindings read the stack's declared capabilities": passed |
| 4 | Author time: `security-anchor-high-privilege` in `validateSecurityPosture`, keyed on `isDefault: true` only | `lint/src/validate-security-posture.ts:940`; registry row `lint/src/authoring-rules.ts:2010-2019` (`gating`, commands `validate`/`build`/`lint`, surfaces `cli` + `runtime-publish`, `runtimeTypes` include `permission`) | an `error` finding on the CLI. At the metadata door's publish it is `422 INVALID_METADATA` (`metadata-protocol/src/runtime-authoring-gate.ts:1194-1195`). Draft saves are not gated | scratch probe below and `validate-security-posture.test.ts` (166 passed) |
| 5 | `guest` | no production caller of the `guest` tier | no door binds a set: the confirm door refuses a `guest` row with `409 SUGGESTION_STATE` (`suggested-audience-bindings.ts:1009`), and the sync never produces one | test "refuses a guest-anchor row loudly rather than record a grant it does not deliver": passed |
| 6 | The anchor seal (any set, high-privilege or not) | package door: `objectql/src/security-catalog-namespace.ts:122` `BUILT_IN_SECURITY_CATALOG_NAMES`; metadata door: the sealed-managed-item refusal at `metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts:18279` | package door: refused. Metadata door: `403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE` | `registry-security-catalog-namespace.test.ts` "the built-in holders" (9 passed, `position everyone` among them). The metadata-door half is pinned for `guest` by `packages/qa/dogfood/test/guest-grants-channel.dogfood.test.ts:479-491`, which I read and did not run (it needs the whole-workspace dogfood boot). `everyone` goes through the same predicate, which I also read and did not run |

No engine (data-layer) write gate on anchor bindings remains: the plugin-security write gates mention no anchor refusal. `delegated-admin-gate.ts` `ANCHOR_POSITIONS` refuses `sys_user_position` assignments to an anchor, which is a user assignment and not a set binding. The `/security/_activation` door refuses switching an anchor (`400`), which is not a binding either.

**Scratch probe** (not committed; run with `tsx` against `packages/lint/src` over the built closure). Calls `runRuntimeAuthoringRules({ type: 'permission', item })` and `validateSecurityPosture({ permissions: [item] })`:

```text
runtime rules for permission: validateRetiredPermissionResidue,validateSecurityPosture,validateSecurityRoleWord,validateRlsPredicateEnforceability
isDefault_with_delete {"runtimeErrors":["security-anchor-high-privilege"],"runtimeAdvisories":[],"cliFindings":["security-anchor-high-privilege:error"]}
isDefault_read_only {"runtimeErrors":[],"runtimeAdvisories":[],"cliFindings":[]}
not_default_with_delete {"runtimeErrors":[],"runtimeAdvisories":[],"cliFindings":[]}
```
